title: Come You Sinners Poor and Wretched
lyrics_original: Come, you sinners, poor and wretched,
Weak and wounded, sick and sore;
Jesus ready stands to save you,
Full of pity, joined with pow'r.
I will arise and go to Jesus,
He will embrace me in His arms;
In the arms of my dear Savior,
O there are ten thousand charms.
Come, you thirsty, come, and welcome,
God's free bounty glorify;
True belief and true repentance,
Every grace that brings you nigh.
I will arise and go to Jesus,
He will embrace me in His arms;
In the arms of my dear Savior,
O there are ten thousand charms.
Come, you weary, heavy laden,
Bruised and broken by the fall;
If you tarry till you're better,
You will never come at all.
I will arise and go to Jesus,
He will embrace me in His arms;
In the arms of my dear Savior,
O there are ten thousand charms.
View Him prostrate in the garden;
On the ground your Maker lies.
On the bloody tree behold Him;
Sinner, will this not suffice?
I will arise and go to Jesus,
He will embrace me in His arms;
In the arms of my dear Savior,
O there are ten thousand charms.
Lo! Th'incarnate God ascended,
Pleads the merit of His blood:
Venture on Him, venture wholly,
Let no other trust intrude.
I will arise and go to Jesus,
He will embrace me in His arms;
In the arms of my dear Savior,
O there are ten thousand charms.
Let not conscience make you linger,
Nor of fitness fondly dream;
All the fitness He requireth
Is to feel your need of Him.
I will arise and go to Jesus,
He will embrace me in His arms;
In the arms of my dear Savior,
O there are ten thousand charms.

bible_verses.english: “Come to me, all you who labor and are heavily burdened, and I will give you rest.
I will get up and go to my father, and will tell him, ‘Father, I have sinned against heaven, and in your sight.
But God commends his own love toward us, in that while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.

devotional.prayer_english: Lord Jesus, thank You for welcoming me even when I feel poor, wounded, and weary. I choose to arise and run into Your waiting arms today, trusting in Your mercy and power to heal me. Help me to stop striving to fix myself and instead receive Your free, abundant grace. In Your loving presence, my heart finds rest and true joy. Amen.

devotional.reflection_english: This classic hymn offers a gentle, open invitation to bring our brokenness directly to Jesus without waiting to clean ourselves up first. He does not turn away the weak or weary; instead, His arms are open wide with immense pity and full saving power. When we make the decision to arise and go to Him, we discover a Savior whose grace is far sweeter than anything this world offers. Come just as you are, thirsty and needy, and rest in His rich welcome.
